feed.title: The Tesla Dispatch
feed.subtitle: Weekday briefing on Tesla's cars, autonomy, robots, energy and stock
feed.rights: The Tesla Dispatch is an independent weekday digest of public news, X posts, regulatory filings and market data about Tesla, Inc., and is not affiliated with the company. Quotes are verbatim; emoji in quoted posts are omitted for print. Market data are delayed and may be revised. Not investment advice.

entry.title: Friday, October 23, 2026: A special committee, in writing
entry.summary:
"The Tesla board of directors has formed a special committee (the 'Special Committee') comprising disinterested directors to explore deepening Tesla's relationship with SpaceX, which could be through certain arrangements including without limitation a business combination," Tesla says in its third-quarter 10-Q, filed late Wednesday. "While there could be merits to a Transaction, there is no assurance that any such Transaction will be consummated," it adds; any deal would need the committee's recommendation and any required shareholder approval. SpaceX's own 10-Q, filed at 4:03 p.m. EDT Thursday, says its board has formed a committee too and that "no determination" has been made.

The shares fell 3.08% to $374.58 on Thursday after Tesla cut its 2026 capital spending forecast to about $20 billion from more than $25 billion, "raising concerns among investors counting on heavy investment for Elon Musk's AI and robotics vision," Reuters reported. "The risk is Tesla now enters a period of limbo while investors await news on a potential combination with SpaceX," AJ Bell's Russ Mould told the agency. At least nine brokers raised their price targets on Thursday, Yahoo Finance data show.

entry.title: Thursday, October 22, 2026: A beat, a cash surprise and a $20 billion budget
entry.summary:
Tesla earned an adjusted 48 cents a share in the third quarter on revenue of $28.05 billion, ahead of the 43 cents and $27.9 billion analysts polled by LSEG expected, CNBC reported. GAAP net income fell 43% to $787 million, or 22 cents a share, while free cash flow was a positive $1.53 billion, according to Tesla's shareholder update, filed with the SEC at 4:41 p.m. EDT Wednesday.

"After many years of grind and things being fairly flat, I think we are now headed for a lot of fun and significant growth," Elon Musk said on the webcast (transcript). The shares, which rose 3.41% to $386.47 in Wednesday's session, slid more than 3% in extended trading, CNBC reported, and were down about 4% in premarket trading on Thursday, according to CNBC.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 21, 2026: Results day, with a merger in the air
entry.summary:
Tesla reports its third quarter after Wednesday's close. The night before, on SpaceX's earnings webcast, Elon Musk said Tesla and SpaceX have each formed special committees of independent directors to study a merger at the request of shareholders, and that he is staying out of their talks as "a conflicted party," The Guardian reported. No terms have been agreed.

TSLA rose 1.54% to $373.71 on Tuesday, the best showing among the "Magnificent Seven" megacaps, Investopedia reported, and gained another 1.2% after hours, according to Bloomberg Law.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 20, 2026: Results tomorrow, and a new FSD build today
entry.summary:
Tesla reports its third quarter after Wednesday's close. The 23 analysts in the company's own compiled consensus, posted Monday, expect $28.34 billion in revenue, 45 cents a share in adjusted earnings and negative free cash flow of $4.51 billion as capital spending runs near $7.8 billion. On Tuesday the company began rolling out software update 2026.38.5.10 with FSD (Supervised) v14.3.13 for AI4 cars and v14.3 Lite for HW3, Not a Tesla App lists.

In a letter filed Monday evening, the board asked shareholders to re-elect Elon Musk, Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel and said FSD now has nearly 1.5 million paid customers. TSLA rose 3.76% to $368.06 on Monday as AI stocks rebounded and Tesla gave the consumer sector its second-biggest lift, Reuters reported.

entry.title: Monday, October 19, 2026: A December vote on Musk, Denholm and Straubel
entry.summary:
Tesla filed its proxy before dawn Monday: shareholders meet December 3 at Gigafactory Texas to re-elect Elon Musk, chair Robyn Denholm and JB Straubel, cast an advisory vote on 2025 pay and ratify the auditor, according to the DEF 14A. There is no merger proposal, despite a prediction market putting the odds of a Tesla-SpaceX deal before March at 56%, CNBC reported.

Over the weekend, Slovakia cleared FSD (Supervised) and Austin robotaxi rides were extended to midnight. Musk wrote that "Optimus and Cybercab will be the vast majority of Tesla's value." TSLA fell 2.13% to $354.72 on Friday as the Nasdaq dropped, and third-quarter results come Wednesday.

entry.title: Friday, October 16, 2026: The Roadster flies, and it is two years away
entry.summary:
Tesla's new Roadster drove up a towering curved ramp, hung upside down on fan suction, flipped in the air on SpaceX cold-gas thrusters and later hopped over a Cybercab, Cybertruck, Semi, Model Y and Model 3 at a SpaceX test site in McGregor, Texas, on Thursday night, Reuters reported. A timed run reached 60 mph in a claimed 0.81 seconds. Musk said production starts in 2028. "Turns out the future does have flying cars," he posted.

No price was given. Tesla is taking $50,000 deposits for the Performance version and $250,000 for Thrust; Rocket is invite-only. TSLA slipped 1.29% to $362.44 before the show and was up 5% in premarket trading Friday, according to Reuters. Third-quarter results come Wednesday.

entry.title: Thursday, October 15, 2026: Roadster night: the livestream starts at 8:55 p.m. EDT
entry.summary:
Tesla shows its new Roadster tonight near Waco, Texas, nearly nine years after the first reveal. "The new Tesla Roadster is a candidate for greatest product demo of all time," Elon Musk posted late Wednesday, and later added that the demo "will be a BANGER, probably metaphorically, though some chance literally." Tesla's own account asked, "Anything happening tomorrow?"

FSD (Supervised) v14.3 Lite is reaching older Hardware 3 Model S and Model X cars for the first time. TSLA fell 2.15% to $367.16 as a hotter-than-expected inflation report sent the Nasdaq 100 down 2.02%. Tesla has filed nothing new with the SEC.

entry.title: Wednesday, October 14, 2026: Roadster goes live Thursday night; HW3 cars get a distilled FSD
entry.summary:
Tesla has set a start time for the Roadster demonstration: the livestream begins Thursday at 7:55 p.m. Central, 8:55 p.m. EDT, Tesla posted on Tuesday night. Elon Musk added: "Timing is everything." Release notes for software 2026.38.5.1 describe a version of FSD (Supervised) for older Hardware 3 (HW3) cars trained using the newer HW4 software as a guide.

US Model 3 and Model Y buyers can now power their homes from the car in an outage with Powershare Home Backup. In Canada, the cheaper China-built Model 3 is off the order page until March 2027. TSLA slipped 0.74% to $375.23 on about half its usual volume. Tesla has filed nothing new with the SEC.

entry.title: Tuesday, October 13, 2026: FSD becomes "Tesla Assisted Driving" in Europe, as regulators look at school-zone speeding
entry.summary:
Tesla has renamed Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) "Tesla Assisted Driving" on its European websites, meeting a condition set by Germany's transport minister, who now says he will push for approval across the European Union (EU). In the US, the National Highway Traffic Safety Administration (NHTSA) has opened a file on a petition alleging that Tesla robotaxis sped through active school zones, and estimates the fleet at about 1,000 vehicles. Tesla's Robotaxi account said service now runs from 6 a.m. to 11 p.m. and that Grok Bot is available in the Cybercab.

A Cybercab from the Austin fleet was unveiled at the Paris Motor Show's press day on Monday; the public gets in from today. A Taiwanese power company disclosed an order for 260 Megapacks, and Tesla is offering free Supercharging in three Florida Panhandle cities hit by Hurricane Isaias. TSLA fell 1.22% to $378.03 on light volume. Tesla has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC). The Roadster demonstration is Thursday.

entry.title: Monday, October 12, 2026: 300 Cybercabs in Austin and "Dallas soon," a new FSD build, and a week of Paris and the Roadster ahead
entry.summary:
Tesla's Robotaxi account said on Saturday that more than 300 Cybercabs now serve Austin, eight times as many as a month ago, and Tesla's head of AI software, Ashok Elluswamy, added "Dallas soon." An independent tracker counted 105 Cybercabs in unsupervised service the same day. Software 2026.38.5, carrying Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) v14.3.12 for newer cars and v14.3 Lite for Hardware 3, began reaching owners on Saturday. Slovakia is still preparing the letter that would make it the ninth European Union (EU) country to allow the system.

Speaking by video at the fan-run X Takeover at Giga Texas, Elon Musk said Tesla aims to produce ten chip designs a year and that China's magnet export ban set Optimus back two to three months. The stock rose 2.05% to $382.70 on Friday, ahead of the S&P 500's 0.59% gain. The Paris Motor Show runs through Sunday, the new Roadster is unveiled Thursday, and third-quarter results follow on October 21. Tesla has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Friday morning.

entry.title: Friday, October 9, 2026: Full Self-Driving gets a new European name, Texas adds 150 Cybercabs overnight, and Shanghai posts its best month of 2026
entry.summary:
Tesla's European websites now sell Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) as "Tesla Assisted Driving," a rename that follows talks with Germany's transport ministry, which has promised to back European Union (EU) approval in a vote expected no earlier than December. In Texas, Tesla added a record 150 Cybercabs to the state's automated-vehicle registry in a single batch, nearly doubling the purpose-built robotaxi's count to 319. Lemonade extended its FSD insurance discount to older Hardware 3 cars running the new v14 Lite.

China's passenger car association said Tesla sold 95,366 China-made cars in September, its highest monthly total this year, as exports from Shanghai rose 58%. Pilot and Tesla opened their first shared Megacharger site for the Tesla Semi in Georgia, and Elon Musk received the National Medal of Science at the White House. The stock eased 0.74% to $375.00 on Thursday while the Nasdaq 100 fell 1.39%. Tesla has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Thursday morning; third-quarter results arrive October 21.

entry.title: Thursday, October 8, 2026: Model Y rules Europe's September charts, Slovakia readies Full Self-Driving, and Dan Ives returns with a $500 target
entry.summary:
Wednesday's news came mostly from Europe. Tesla said the Model Y was the best-selling passenger car in all five Nordic countries in September, and German registration data showed it outsold the Volkswagen Golf by about 22%. Slovakia's transport minister said the country would approve Full Self-Driving (FSD) (Supervised) "within days," which would make it the ninth European Union (EU) country to do so, as a new FSD build, v14.3.11, began reaching owners. Tesla will also show a Cybercab and an Optimus robot at the Paris Motor Show next week.

On Wall Street, Dan Ives made Tesla his first call at his new firm, Yorkville Ives, with an Outperform rating and a $500 price target, and UBS raised its target to $391. The stock still slipped 0.75% to $377.81 on light volume, ending a three-day winning streak. In energy, more than 85,000 California Powerwalls sent over 600 megawatts (MW) to the grid in a record virtual power plant event, and the first Semi Megacharger on the East Coast opened near Atlanta. Tesla has filed nothing new with the Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) since Wednesday morning; third-quarter results arrive October 21.
